messages:
maria: Quick sync — sales pushed back asking for a clearer migration runway + SLA language before we lock the catalog rollout for their enterprise cohort. Can we agree on acceptance gates today?
varun: I can outline technical gates. thinking: perf parity (p95 < 600ms for typical prompt set), quality delta <= 1.5% on customer evals, and fallback path for pinned customers.
lex: +1. Also need a cost cap suggestion for customers on Dedicated vs Hosted. Sales wants numbers to commit to.
olivia: For quality delta, do we use our standard stability harness or the customer-specific prompt set? They asked about per-customer baselines.
maria: They want per-customer baselines for the 3 largest accounts. We should offer a standard baseline + voluntary per-customer benchmarking for an SLA credit.
jim: Ops concern: if we promise fallback we need autoscaling playbook and a throttling policy. who owns the fallout runbook?
varun: I can own the fallback routing policy (auto-route to stable-pin on congestion) and the KV cache compatibility check. Needs signoff from eng-platform for rollout automation.
lex: For cost caps: preliminary numbers — Hosted: 30% premium over dedicated list price for guaranteed latency; Dedicated: committed flat rate + overage. I'll draft a table.
olivia: On the benchmark side, proposed test harness:
```
- sample size: 2k prompts per customer cohort
- metrics: p50,p95 latency, tokens per response, top-1 quality score, corrected hallucination rate
- run: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with regression checks at each step
```
maria: Good. Also need rollback criteria: any of these triggers rollback: quality drop > 2.5% absolute, p95 increase > 2x baseline, or customer error surge > 3x.
varun: Agree but can we add a lenient early-warning threshold (soft alarms) that escalates instead of auto-rollback for small infra blips?
jim: yes — soft alarm window 15 minutes; if sustained 3 samples -> hard rollback.
lex: Sales asks for SLA wording: "95th latency below X ms for pinned versions; service credit if missed for > 3 consecutive days." We need legal + finance to weigh in.
maria: I'll loop in legal after we settle numeric thresholds. For X, let's propose p95 <= 600ms for Hosted enterprise, p95 <= 350ms for Dedicated at provisioned throughput.
olivia: We should also define the migration incentive: 90-day discounted pinning for customers who opt into early migration + free per-customer benchmark run.
varun: Operational checklist for onboarding a model to catalog (draft):
1) compatibility smoke (tokenizer, kv layout)
2) perf bench (2k prompts)
3) eval gating (quality + safety checks)
4) pin contract drafted
5) canary automation wired -> telemetry dashboards
6) rollback policy set

We should make each step a checkbox in the catalog UI.
maria: Nice. How about exceptions? BigCorp asked for extended pin TTL and partial-deprecation gracepath. We should offer an "exception" flow with an approval step and extended SLA window.
lex: Exceptions require finance approval and reserve capacity tagging. Also require a sunset timeline in contract. Keep it rare.
jim: On canary automation: @canary-bot can we add a preflight that runs the harness and posts a summary?
canary-bot: scheduled preflight started for model vX. Running 2000-sample perf+quality suite. Will post results to the thread. :robot_face:
canary-bot: preflight complete — p50: 120ms, p95: 420ms, quality delta: -0.9% vs baseline. No safety flags. Link: https://ci.internal/preflight/3543219876
olivia: Those numbers look within the acceptance gates. We should mark this canary as eligible for 10% rollout.
varun: I'll prepare the auto-route rule: if p95 > 700ms or quality delta < -2.0% -> immediate pin fallback. Otherwise proceed with staged rollout.
maria: Final ask: can we publish a short product-facing doc with the migration runway, customer options (pinning, migration assistance, SLA tiers) by EOD tomorrow? Sales needs it for renewal conversations.
lex: I can author the "pricing + cost cap" section. varun/olivia — can you co-author the benchmark & rollback pages?
varun: yes, I'll draft technical appendix.
olivia: I'll own the eval methodology and customer-facing checklist.
jim: I'll add ops playbooks and contact rotation.
maria: Great — I'll collect approvals and ping legal/finance tomorrow morning. If no objections, we'll present this at the GTM sync at 10am PT. :calendar:
lex: ack.
varun: ack.
olivia: ack.
jim: ack.
canary-bot: reminder scheduled for 09:00 PT tomorrow to ping legal/finance.
